findings.evidence: `@[expose] def Hom.mk'` at lines 52-56, while `Hom.toOverHom_mk'` and `Hom.toSchemeHom_mk'` at lines 75-112 already provide the needed API without unfolding the body.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from `Hom.mk'`; keep `Hom.toOverHom_mk'`/`Hom.toSchemeHom_mk'` as the public way to use the constructor, adding more characteristic lemmas if consumers need them.
findings.issue: `Hom.mk'` exposes its body, leaking the nested induced-category/`Grp.homMk''` implementation as part of the public interface even though projection lemmas now characterize the constructor.

findings.evidence: Lines 83-93 declare `@[reassoc] lemma Hom.one_hom` and `@[reassoc] lemma Hom.mul_hom`; Mathlib registers the wrapped lemmas with `attribute ... (attr := reassoc (attr := simp)) IsMonHom.one_hom IsMonHom.mul_hom` in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mon.lean:216`.
findings.fix: Register both wrapper lemmas with the equivalent of `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`/`@[simp, reassoc]` so `simp` normalizes unit and multiplication preservation through `AbelianVariety.Hom`.
findings.issue: `Hom.one_hom` and `Hom.mul_hom` are characteristic normal-form lemmas for the new hom type but are only marked `@[reassoc]`, so the public wrapper does not carry the `simp` automation that the underlying `IsMonHom` API provides.

summary: The homomorphism surface is mostly characterized now, but it still exposes an implementation body and leaves core preservation lemmas under-annotated for the public API.
